parsed.rationale: Both `CacheLoader` (package `Caching`) and `MetadataLoader` (package `Metadata`) share three identical members — `cacheKey:String`, `invalidate:() async`, and `lastLoadedAt:Date?` — and differ only in the return type of `load`: `Data` vs `PlaycutMetadata`. This is the canonical PAT pattern: a single protocol with an `associatedtype Payload` and a requirement `load:() async throws -> Payload` would unify both interfaces, allowing the shared members to be declared once. Introducing `CacheLoadable` in a common shared package (e.g., a new `Shared/CacheCore` or the existing `Caching` package if `Metadata` already depends on it) eliminates the structural duplication while preserving each concrete loader's distinct payload type. Neither record is test, codegen, mock, or sample-app code, so there is no intentionality flag that would block this refactor.
